paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when life is rough, you don't have to fake being fine. Psalm 123 is two songs of ascents, and the first one is honest. The singer says they have "endured much contempt" and asks for mercy twice (Psalm 123:3). Nobody in that song pretends, and the LORD doesn't tell them to.

Now look at where their eyes go. They look to the LORD like servants looking to their master's hand, "until He shows us mercy" (Psalm 123:2). Then David sings that if the LORD had not been on their side, the floods would have engulfed them (Psalm 124:1, 4). I think David is telling us the waiting wasn't wasted. The LORD was on their side the whole time, even before they could see it.

So what do you do with that, baker? You look UP, you ask, and then you tell somebody what He has done, because David wanted a whole crowd saying it with him. When you've slipped out of a snare, you say it out loud: "Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth" (Psalm 124:8). Whatever is on your plate today, the One who made heaven and earth is on your side. Keep your eyes on His hand, and keep a little room in your heart for the praise!
